name: Kaitai Struct
listed_description: A declarative language to describe various binary data structures and a compiler to generate C++ parser code.
reason: Directional claim only. The FAQ (kaitai_struct_doc/faq.adoc) says 'Is it fast? Yes, pretty much. Kaitai Struct is not a runtime interpreter, but a compiler ... Code that it generates is about as fast as one can write in a particular language', with no numbers. The benchmarks submodule (kaitai-io/kaitai_struct_benchmarks) README only describes how to build and run the suite (C++/STL, Python, Ruby) and has no results or baseline. The umbrella repo and C++ runtime README have no performance numbers, and a WebSearch for a protobuf or hand-written parser comparison found none. The seed's guessed protobuf baseline is a different job (schema serialization versus declarative parsing of existing formats). kaitai.io itself was not opened.

name: kdtree
listed_description: Simple library for working with KD-trees.
reason: Directional claim only. README.rst says kd-trees 'facilitate very fast searching' and the implementation is 'designed to be efficient and very easy to use'; doc/index.html, doc/guide.html and doc/install.html contain no benchmark (only a note about a fast result-node allocator). No benchmark directory in the repo, and a WebSearch for shootouts including this library (nanoflann and others) found no row for it. The seed's guessed std::map baseline does not fit a spatial index.

name: levenstein.c
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. The README (readme.md) documents only levenshtein() and levenshtein_n() usage, install and license; the repo has no benchmark, and the only performance mention found by WebSearch is for unrelated JavaScript packages (fastest-levenshtein, fast-levenshtein). No third-party C shootout row for wooorm/levenshtein.c was found. The seed's guessed std::string baseline does not apply to an edit-distance function.

name: libavl
listed_description: Library containing a range of self-balancing binary trees.
reason: No numeric comparison against a recognizable baseline reachable. adtinfo.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the book text could not be read. Search snippets of Ben Pfaff's own performance analysis (libavl abstract, benpfaff.org) compare libavl's tree variants against each other (AVL, red-black, splay, unbalanced BST: AVL up to 20% faster than red-black on real-world VMA traces), not against std::map, GTree or any other external incumbent. No third-party shootout including libavl was found, so there is no number against a named baseline.
